tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Thistledown Studios** is an independent video game developer with 240 employees. The studio runs its player-facing services and its internal build infrastructure in the East US 2 region.

**Current Environment:**
- The player account portal is a web app named **app-portal** that runs in an Azure App Service plan (Premium v3) in the virtual network-adjacent resource group **RG-Player**
- Player profile data is stored in an Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server named **pg-players**, which is injected into the subnet **Subnet-Data** of the virtual network **VNet-Games** and has **no public network access**
- A matchmaking API is being redesigned as a set of small Linux containers
- Roughly 40 Windows build-agent VMs compile game assets; each VM is manually configured from a checklist before it joins the build pool

**Business Requirements:**
- Player-facing services must stay on platform-as-a-service offerings; the studio does not want to operate Kubernetes clusters or patch VM fleets for these workloads
- The build-agent fleet must be rebuilt from a standardized, versioned golden image instead of manual checklists

tabs.title: Compute Detail
tabs.content:
**Portal Database Connectivity (app-portal):**
- app-portal must open **outbound** connections to pg-players on its private IP address inside Subnet-Data
- Inbound traffic to the portal itself remains public and unchanged
- The team has already reserved an empty subnet, **Subnet-AppOut** (10.80.4.0/27), in VNet-Games for whatever the solution needs

**Matchmaking API:**
- Traffic is extremely bursty: near zero at night, thousands of HTTPS requests per second during evening tournaments
- The containers must **scale out automatically on incoming HTTPS request volume** and must **scale in to zero running replicas** when idle so that nothing is billed for compute at night
- The team wants a fully managed service and will not run or upgrade an orchestrator themselves

**Build-Agent Golden Image:**
- A technician has prepared a Windows VM named **VM-AgentBase** with all compilers and SDKs installed
- The image must be published with version numbers (for example 1.0.0, 1.1.0) so that the pool can be rolled back to an earlier image version
- New build agents will be created from the published image in the same subscription
